why_trail.why: Root cause confirmed by reading: membership moved from file CONTENT to file LOCATION at g4, but the non-episode classifier (NON_EPISODE_FILENAMES) stayed at the flat root, so iter_episode_ids promotes active/README.md and retired/README.md to the phantom id 'README'. ID_RE already exists at :113 and rejects 'README', so the store owns a computable classifier; the fix is to apply it in all three directories and move the layout placeholders off .md. Same drift shape as the newline character-list the run already replaced once.

Classifier is derived, not enumerated: episode_id_for() applies the store's own ID_RE to any *.md and is the single membership rule in active/, retired/ and the flat root. A non-episode .md inside a layout directory is REFUSED as malformed rather than promoted to an id. Shipped placeholders moved off .md to .gitkeep so the tracked store is well-formed by the store's own grammar; documentation folded into episodes/README.md. Both test helpers now ask the shipped classifier. Trap 4 (non-episode file inside a layout directory) is named alongside traps 1-3 with its own naive fixture.

Split the create/read asymmetry explicitly: ensure_store_layout() is the writer's bootstrap (apply_delta calls it, so a create into a fresh root still works and a store can come into being), _require_store_layout() is every read seam's first act (iter_episode_ids, resolve_episode_path, is_episode_in_ordinary_search), so a typo'd --store-root or an uncommitted layout is refused instead of answered as empty. Temp stores in the suite now start with the layout, matching the shipped store; the two tests that relied on a layout-less directory were re-pointed at a real-but-empty store, preserving their falsification intent.

Half-retirement is now loud at all three kinds of caller, not just scanners: resolve_episode_path checks BOTH directories and refuses when two exist (so fetch_episode and _Transaction.load inherit it), and apply_delta runs the enumeration seam as a pre-flight before any op, so a retire of an unrelated episode can no longer commit against a store already known corrupt. Documented limit stated rather than hidden: fetch refuses for the affected id and does not scan the whole store per lookup. The three over-claiming docstrings and section 7's 'readers and the writer alike' sentence now describe what the code does, as a per-caller table.

F6 closed in the same scan as F4: both stray detection and the layout scan are now recursive, with depth part of the name test, so a record at episodes/archive/x.md or active/old/x.md is refused rather than omitted; the flat-root allowlist is scoped to the flat root. F7 collapsed into _selectable_field_reader(). Own sweep found a third silent-omission shape the review did not name: enumerate_episodes() dropped any scanned id fetch could not resolve via 'if ep is not None' - now raises, with a test. Also corrected the query CLI's blanket 'corrupt store:' prefix, which was wrong for the store-is-absent case, and gave dry-run the same pre-flight. Docs sections 7 and 10 now describe six traps, the derived classifier, the .gitkeep placeholders and a seven-row seam table.

Every VERIFY command reproduced with pasted output: shipped store enumerates exit 0, create into a fresh --store-root exit 0 and reads back, tests/test_episode_store.py 105 passed 1 skipped, tests/ 1262 passed 3 skipped, all three adversarial fixtures exit 1, git status unchanged in shape. C2 containment still holds (zero directory literals in query_episodes.py; all writer uses inside the seam block, 470-804). Mutation evidence redone by source patch, and it caught a real gap in my own new tests (M6).
